borisTake: This is the rapamycin story I actually care about: not another mouse-lifespan victory lap, but a real attempt to pin down dose, schedule, and biological targets in older humans. I'm bullish on rapa, but if you still can't say daily versus intermittent and where benefit flips into immune or glucose tradeoffs, you're doing protocol cosplay, not medicine.
leadAnalysis: Rapamycin works by inhibiting mTOR, which shifts cells toward autophagy, stress resistance, and altered immune-metabolic tone, but the field has been running far ahead of the human dosing data. What makes this trial important is that it is structured to map biological benchmarks first, then test whether daily versus intermittent dosing can recapture younger immune and metabolic function without dragging patients into transplant-style immunosuppression. That is exactly the bottleneck for serious longevity practice: not whether rapa is mechanistically interesting, but what exposure actually produces useful human effects. Clinically, the 84-person randomized phase should finally start separating evidence-based protocol design from forum folklore.
oneNumber: 50% | Lower all-cause mortality with 15 years of WHO-level activity

papers.title: Academic Clinical Trials for Rapamycin to Answer Questions on Dosing for Anti-Aging Use
papers.summary: UT Health San Antonio is launching a multi-phase rapamycin program that moves from youthful biomarker benchmarking into dose-finding and then an 84-person randomized trial comparing daily dosing, intermittent dosing, and placebo in older adults. For longevity medicine, that matters more than another mouse paper because it targets the actual unanswered question: what human exposure gives mTOR benefit without tipping into immunosuppression or hyperglycemia.
papers.source: Fight Aging! / UT Health San Antonio

papers.title: BCL-2 and Cellular Senescence in Pulmonary Fibrosis
papers.summary: In pulmonary fibrosis, persistent BCL-2 expression kept PDGFRα+ fibroblasts from undergoing apoptosis, allowing senescent, matrix-producing myofibroblasts to accumulate and lock lungs into pathological remodeling. Venetoclax re-opened the apoptotic program in fibrotic mice, reduced senescence, and promoted fibrosis resolution, making fibrotic disease look like a more tractable senolytic target than the field has treated it.

papers.title: APOE4 Increases Neurons’ Excitability Before Symptoms Appear
papers.summary: Nature Aging data show neuronal APOE4 pushes CA3 hippocampal neurons into a smaller, hyperexcitable state long before cognitive symptoms emerge, and early interictal spike burden predicted later spatial learning decline. Knocking down Nell2 reversed the cellular phenotype in adult mice, which turns APOE4 from a static risk marker into a potentially druggable circuit-level target.

papers.title: uPAR Targeting to Enable CAR T Cell Therapies to Treat Solid Cancers
papers.summary: uPAR-targeted CAR-T cells attack not just tumor cells but the wound-healing, fibrotic support niche around them, which is exactly why the approach looks more relevant to solid tumors than classic lineage-targeted CAR-Ts. uPAR was elevated in 12 of 14 human cancer types examined, and in ovarian cancer models the therapy wiped out metastases and produced durable remissions.

papers.title: A Target for Ameliorating Post-Operative Delirium
papers.summary: In aged MCI rats, anaesthetic surgery drove microglia toward glycolysis, inflammation, ATP depletion, and stress-granule buildup, while suppressing RUVBL2 reversed much of that cascade and improved cognition. Since postoperative delirium can accelerate long-term decline in older brains, this makes microglial metabolic reprogramming look like a much better target than treating delirium as a transient peri-operative nuisance.

papers.title: Physical Activity Correlates With a Sizable Difference to Late Life Mortality
papers.summary: An emulated-trial analysis of 11,169 Australian women found that sustaining at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous activity over 15 years was associated with a 50% lower all-cause mortality risk versus persistent non-adherence. The interesting part is not that exercise is good — everybody knows that — but how large the late-life survival gap remains even when analyzed through a more causal lens.

papers.title: Proposing Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure to be Manifestations of the Same Condition
papers.summary: New work argues that reduced TBX5 expression may sit upstream of both atrial fibrillation and heart failure, with overlapping transcriptional disruption across more than 100 regulators. If that holds up, cardiac aging starts to look less like separate rhythm and pump disorders and more like one shared atrial failure program with a cleaner upstream intervention point.

papers.title: A Review Focused on Exerkines in Extracellular Vesicles Generated by Muscle Tissue
papers.summary: This review sharpens the exerkine story by focusing on exercise-induced extracellular vesicles as the cargo system carrying muscle-derived benefits into adipose tissue, immune networks, and stem-cell niches. The translational angle is obvious: if the field can standardize these vesicles, some exercise biology may eventually become harvestable and engineerable instead of purely behavioral.
papers.source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology / Fight Aging!
